locations.name: Stormgate
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation. The well cover bears the names of three households, though only two remain on this road. A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.

locations.name: Gloamwick
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes. A narrow stair beneath the market ends at the door of the former mint. Nobody has removed its seals. A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.

locations.name: The Flint Weald
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts. Charcoal pits lie under the fern beds. A rusted pan still hangs from a keeper’s shelter. A promise is repeated in the listener’s own words.

locations.name: Ravenbridge Reliquary

Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny. A row of empty hooks remains beside the entrance; the wall beneath each is lighter than the stone around it. Guests leave a small candle at the public hearth.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Gloamwick, necromancy is permitted; in Stormgate, it is forbidden; in Cinderwold, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.

history.text: Isca Morrowward has made a small fort from packing crates. Ysol Oakwatch tells the younger children it is full, although there is a whole bench inside. Your sibling taps twice on the gate and waits. You know the game they are playing; you also know who owns the crates.

history.title: A second hand in the margins
history.text: Ysol Ironveil lends you a lesson book. The careful diagrams are in Riven Cindermoor's hand, but Ysol Ironveil has written their own name on the cover. “We worked together,” Ysol Ironveil says, closing the book before you reach the last page. Riven Cindermoor is waiting outside the classroom.

history.title: The chair left in the aisle
history.text: Ysol Ironveil arrives carrying a chair that Ysol Reedwick lent months ago. Neither remembers who first stopped visiting. The chair is set in the aisle between their doors. “It was never about the chair,” Ysol Reedwick says, but does not take it inside.

history.title: One name on the hanging sign
history.text: Sorra Morrowward and Tutor Enna Iron have spent three evenings preparing a display for the market. When the cloth comes down, only Sorra Morrowward's mark is visible. Tutor Enna Iron wipes a thumb across the empty corner. “The paint was wet when I left,” they say.

history.title: An empty place in the rehearsal
history.text: Ysol Oakwatch has rehearsed the first verse all week. Merek Gravemere tells the others that Ysol Oakwatch will not be coming, then starts practicing the solo. Through the doorway you can see Ysol Oakwatch carrying a basket home. The lantern procession leaves at dusk.

history.title: The names on the invitation
history.text: Sorra Morrowward invites you to a small supper behind the old bell tower. Ysol Ironveil's name is missing from the folded list. “It is not a quarrel,” Sorra Morrowward says. “I just want one evening without an argument.” Ysol Ironveil has asked what you are doing tonight.

history.title: The stones at the garden edge
history.text: Isca Morrowward has moved a row of boundary stones beside the shared path. Riven Cindermoor puts them back every morning. Today they have both arrived with a bucket, and neither can reach the well without passing the other. A page from an old lease flaps beneath the nearest stone.

history.title: The certificate folded small
history.text: Isca Morrowward receives a certificate before the assembled hall. Ysol Reedwick, who practiced with them for weeks, slips outside before the applause ends. Later Isca Morrowward asks why Ysol Reedwick will not come to the supper. The certificate is folded small enough to fit a coat pocket.

choices.label: Put both names on the account
choices.outcome: You keep the field marks and share authorship. Your rival agrees to compare later discoveries without promising agreement.

choices.label: Inspect the original terms and witnesses
choices.outcome: You copy the amount and ask a living witness what was agreed. No new debt or hereditary obligation is accepted.
